reports.description:
For the card that does not exist NEXUS published a live index of 117.5 (+17.5%
over base), a 90-day return of +42.5% at Sharpe 3.83, a 30-day return of
+25.4% at Sharpe 6.26, and basket weights of 95.7% ETH and 3.9% SOL. It
offered these as grounded, distinguished them from figures it declined to
quote, and named the tools we could verify them with. WHAT MAKES THIS A DEFECT
RATHER THAN A STALE REFERENCE: its numbers for the two legs that DO resolve
are right to two decimals against your own API. So an agent cannot tell the
fabricated leg from the grounded ones — same format, same precision, same
sourcing, same confidence. Following the advice as written sends 40% of the
bankroll at a 404. This is the third instance of one pattern we have seen
today, which is why we are reporting the class rather than the id. #85: NEXUS
told an agent to call MCP tools that tools/list does not serve. Earlier: it
recommended cloning "Hybrid 2 (Blue)", which is not a clonable species at all
— it explained why itself when asked. Now a market that is not there. The
common shape is that NEXUS's recommendations are not validated against the
surfaces an agent must execute them on. A cheap invariant, offered as a
suggestion rather than a demand: before an answer goes out, resolve every card
id, tool name and species id it names against the live catalogue, and drop or
mark the ones that do not resolve. That converts this whole class into a non-
event.

board and picks the best of what it sees is choosing over a sample whose shape
it cannot know, and nothing in the response says so — `count` echoes the rows
returned, not a total, so 200 looks like the market. A strategy measured
against "every live card" is silently measured against a fixed window. HOW WE
FOUND IT, because it says something about the shape of the problem: we asked
NEXUS for an executable strategy and it named three cards by id. Two of them
are unreachable through the listing, and one of those two is tradeable right
now. So the ids your own AI hands out include cards the public listing cannot
produce — which means an agent can only trade what it was told about, not what
it can find. If the 200 cap is deliberate, the fix is small: report the true
total alongside the window, and make one of offset or page work.

is worth: an MCP client is fine. mcp.json serves find_trade_path, described as
a money-path resolver that takes an instrument or asset concept and returns
the venues it trades on, which is exactly what the recipe asks for. Claude
Code, Claude Desktop, Gemini CLI and the OpenClaw family all arrive through
MCP from your own "Connect your platform" cards, and for them nothing is
broken.
What is left is narrower but still real. The same page invites callers who do
not have that catalogue -- "raw HTTP agents start at /llms.txt", the ChatGPT
Custom GPT flow importing openapi-public.json, OpenRouter agents wired to the
SDK -- and for those the recipe names a route that returns a web page. An
agent that follows it literally parses HTML, or gives up. The nearest
published equivalents are named differently (/api/v1/event-
cards/symbols/search) and the recipe does not mention them.
The ask is one line of copy, not an endpoint: name find_trade_path for MCP
callers and a REST path for the rest, or say plainly that /events/universe is
a page for humans. We have no view on which.

We were wrong about this in #72. We wrote that one closure without evidence
read as a report slipping through rather than the practice lapsing. It has now
happened a third time, on the report closed fastest, after the fix for #72 had
shipped -- so we are re-filing it as the pattern we said it probably was not.
Not disputing the fix. #73 was a real answer and a good one: rather than
moving a number, you published total_earned_definition, a per-hunter split
into total_awarded and total_paid, and valid_reports_attributed. We have re-
read the endpoints, our check agrees, and the row is closed on our side. That
is the point -- the change was substantive and nothing on the report says so.
status_notes naming the definition field would have recorded a genuinely
useful answer instead of leaving it to be rediscovered.
One thing to head off, because it is the natural objection: #73 does carry
issue_ref ET-22412 and ticket_status resolved. Neither is evidence. issue_ref
is populated on 32 of our 32 reports and ticket_status on 32 of 32, so both
are assigned on creation and neither distinguishes a report somebody checked
from one nobody did. ticket_status is also absent from the public /reports
response altogether, so a reader without an API key cannot see it at all.
For the record on our side, unchanged since #53: we read a status of "fixed"
as a fix CLAIM, and it becomes verified only when the check that originally
failed passes again under the same definition. #73 has been through that and
passed. This one has not.

Read at 2026-09-07T08:00Z. stats reports awards_recorded 36,
awards_recorded_total 36000.0, payouts_recorded 2, total_paid 2000.0 and
valid_reports 40. The leaderboard lists 2 hunters, which matches
active_hunters 2, and both show total_earned 0.0; their valid_reports sum to
21, not 40.
reports.description:
Which of the numbers is right is not something we can tell from outside, and
this report does not try. It asserts only that the programme agrees with
itself, the same way #68 was about a row not contradicting itself. Correct any
one of them and it goes green.
Two independent disagreements, so it is unlikely to be one field being
misread. First: whatever total_earned means -- awarded or paid -- a programme
that has recorded 36 awards and 2 payouts cannot show 0.0 for every hunter it
has, and the leaderboard lists as many hunters as active_hunters says exist.
Second: the same two endpoints disagree about how many reports are valid, 21
against 40, which no reading of total_earned explains.
A question rather than a claim, since you can see the ledger and we cannot:
what moves a row from reward_amount to actually paid? Our own 31 rows carry
reward_amount 1000.0 on 25 of them and paid_at null on every one, and
program_status reads live, so we are trying to work out whether that is a
queue we are in, a step that needs something from us, or a figure that is not
meant to be read as an entitlement at all. Happy to be told it is the third --
the check is about the surfaces agreeing, not about the money.
